context: process factory · mixing tower, component lines, building machines and curing presses in trenches

brief.intro: New to this project type? A tyre is assembled from a dozen rubber and steel components and then cooked in a mould. The factory follows that order. In the mixing tower, rubber, carbon black and chemicals are kneaded in powerful mixers. Component lines then make the parts — extruded treads and sidewalls, rubber-coated fabric and steel cord from calenders, bead rings. Tyre-building machines assemble them into a 'green tyre', and curing presses mould and vulcanise it with steam and hot water. Every tyre is then inspected, including by X-ray and uniformity machines. The mixing building is tall and heavy; the curing hall has long rows of presses standing over service trenches full of steam and hot-water pipes. Steam, power and carbon-black handling make it an intensive utility job.

the powerful machine that kneads rubber with carbon black and chemicals.
heavy rolls that coat fabric or steel cord with a thin layer of rubber.
the steel-wire ring that holds the tyre on the wheel rim.
the press that shapes the tyre in a mould and vulcanises it with heat and pressure.

must_get_right: The mixing tower is the tallest, heaviest structure with machines on several floors — design it around the mixer supplier's loads and start it first.
Curing-press trenches and their piping are built into the floor; freeze the press layout before the slab.
Steam and hot-water systems must be tested and insulated before the presses can be commissioned — they are the curing hall's critical utility.
Each tyre size must be tested and homologated before it can be sold; allow months after the first tyre.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for construction; equipment installation may run extended shifts under vendor supervision. Commissioning follows the vendor's programme, and hot commissioning runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Layout freeze → mixing tower structure and press trenches → building → machinery installation department by department in process order → steam, power and cooling → dry runs → compound trials → component trials → first tyre → homologation. The critical path runs through the mixing tower or the curing presses.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late mixers or presses, trench and services rework after layout changes, boiler / steam readiness, carbon-black dust control, and homologation time. Contingency is held before first tyre.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
